successCriteria.description: The Notification entity is defined in src/modules/notification/notification.model.ts with exactly the canonical fields id, recipientId, type, title, message, relatedEntityType, relatedEntityId, status, createdAt, readAt (status typed as NotificationStatus, relatedEntityType/relatedEntityId/readAt nullable).
NotificationRepository implements the canonical contract create, findByRecipient, findByEntity, updateStatus, markRead using raw pg parameterized SQL against the shared pool (no Knex in queries).
markRead persists status=READ and readAt=now for the target notification and returns the updated entity; updateStatus persists an arbitrary valid NotificationStatus transition.
NotificationService is a thin delegating facade over the repository with an injectable repository defaulting to the concrete class, exposing the repository operations.

Jest unit tests exist under tests/unit/modules/notification/ covering create, findByRecipient, findByEntity, updateStatus, markRead, and the optional-client write path (mocking src/shared/db pool.query).

constraints: No background fanout: no BullMQ, no queue, no scheduler. bullmq is not a project dependency and must not be added.
Raw pg parameterized SQL only; Knex is migrations-only and must never appear in repository queries.
Write methods accept an optional client?: PoolClient as the LAST parameter and use conn = client ?? pool; read methods use the shared pool.
No `any`: use unknown + type guards. Notification has no jsonb fields, so Record<string, any> is not permitted.
id and createdAt are generated by the repository (randomUUID() / new Date()); never caller-supplied.
Module exposes a public entry point (index.ts); other modules import notification only through it, never internals.
outOfScope: Background notification fanout / delivery (BullMQ, schedulers, push/email transport).
HTTP controller/routes and RBAC wiring for notifications (no API surface this phase).
The leave service's fanout orchestration that will call NotificationService (Phase 8).

entityInvariants.invariant: Lifecycle states are PENDING → SENT → READ → ARCHIVED (NotificationStatus). A notification is created PENDING; readAt is null until the notification is marked read, at which point status becomes READ and readAt is set to the read time.
relatedEntityType and relatedEntityId are either both null (a standalone notification) or both non-null (a notification about a specific entity); they are never mixed.
recipientId references an existing employee (FK recipient_id -> employees.id); a notification is always addressed to exactly one recipient.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Persists a new notification (status defaults to PENDING, id/createdAt generated) and returns the created entity; accepts an optional PoolClient to join a caller's transaction.
Returns all notifications for a recipient, ordered by createdAt descending; returns an empty array when none exist (never throws).
Returns notifications matching a related entity type + id; returns an empty array when none exist (never throws).

Transitions a notification to a supplied valid NotificationStatus and returns the updated entity; throws a typed not-found error (stable machine code) when no row matches; accepts an optional PoolClient.
Sets status=READ and readAt=now for the target notification and returns the updated entity; throws a typed not-found error when no row matches; accepts an optional PoolClient.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse the NotificationStatus enum (PENDING | SENT | READ | ARCHIVED) from src/shared/types/leave.types.ts; do not redeclare it.
Import the shared pg Pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts (via src/shared/db index); never create a second pool or import pg directly for the connection.
Import RepositoryError and UniqueConstraintError from the employee module's public entry point (src/modules/employee/index.ts); do not redeclare them locally.
Match the repository contract INotificationRepository { create, findByRecipient, findByEntity, updateStatus, markRead } declared in the reconciled architecture.

Match the notifications table shape (id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at; PK id; FK recipient_id -> employees.id) and snake_case column mapping.
Follow the established module file structure and conventions (model, repository with interface+class, service.interface, service, errors, index) mirroring the balance module.

integrationPoints.why: The notification entity's status field is typed against this shared enum.
The repository issues all SQL against this single shared pool.
Notification-specific errors extend the shared RepositoryError; unique-violation mapping reuses UniqueConstraintError.
The leave service will call NotificationService to fan out submitted/approved/rejected events; this phase only provides the callable surface.
